arithmetic_proof.accepted_zero_length_case: H264GetNextNALUnit accepts zero-length units; with p=1 and N=S, O=H+4*S while C=2*S, so O>C for every S>0
arithmetic_proof.declared_extent_failure: before calling the helper, the caller does not require p+declared_length <= true_remaining; it uses p+declared_length to invent the helper end, so a declared extent past the socket body can be accepted and copied before the late cumulative-consumption comparison
arithmetic_proof.first_frame_header_case: independently, the unchecked initial memcpy crosses C whenever H>C before NAL conversion begins
arithmetic_proof.important_correction: this exact socket path does not establish a size-doubling integer wrap on x86-64; the demonstrated defects are true-input-bound and output-capacity accounting failures
arithmetic_proof.partial_prefix_failure: because the outer loop continues while at least one byte remains, p=2 or p=4 can read a truncated final prefix beyond the true body before any helper check

output_capacity.growth_allocation: when growth is required, 0x13641 computes 2*S, operator new[] receives that value at 0x136a3, and 0x1372b stores the same value as capacity
output_capacity.growth_test: 0x1361f computes 2*S and compares it with retained capacity at context+0xa8
output_capacity.no_route_local_doubling_wrap: for S <= 0xffffffff, 2*S <= 0x1fffffffe, so the 64-bit doubling does not wrap on this route
output_capacity.upstream_width: the exact socket route supplies a uint32 body size zero-extended into the x86-64 size_t argument

retained_state.configuration: ScreenStreamSetAVCC converts bounded AVCC configuration and stores the Annex-B header pointer at context+0x80, header length H at +0x88, and length-prefix width p at +0x90
retained_state.initialization: ScreenStreamInitialize calls calloc(1,0xc8), so output pointer, capacity, retained AVCC state, and first-frame state begin zeroed
retained_state.start: ScreenStreamStart stores 1 at context+0x98, selecting the one-time retained-header prepend on the next processed frame

socket_to_parser.body_size: 0x1f4f6 loads the uint32 field at session+0x48 and 0x1f502 allocates that many body bytes
socket_to_parser.boundary: the read is from the already-established screen NetSocket; listener creation, pairing, authentication, encryption state, and live peer control are not established here
socket_to_parser.header: 0x1f4b9 requests exactly 0x80 bytes into the retained AirPlayScreenHeader at session+0x48
socket_to_parser.video_config: opcode 1 reaches ScreenStreamSetAVCC@plt at 0x1f7ca when body size is nonzero
socket_to_parser.video_frame: opcode 0 reaches ScreenStreamProcessData@plt at 0x1f747 with the body pointer and uint32 body size

writes_without_output_bound.bounded_helper_scope: H264GetNextNALUnit restricts p to 1, 2, or 4 and bounds each NAL against the end pointer it is given, but that end is synthetic here; it also accepts length zero and returns an input pointer advanced by p
writes_without_output_bound.config_prepend: when context+0x98 is 1, 0x13776..0x1379f copies H retained bytes to the output and advances output-used by H without comparing H with capacity
writes_without_output_bound.declared_extent: 0x13849..0x13911 reads the next p-byte declared NAL length before checking true remaining bytes; 0x139c2 computes p+length and 0x139eb forms a synthetic end pointer from that declared extent
writes_without_output_bound.helper_boundary_mismatch: 0x13a2c passes the synthetic end to H264GetNextNALUnit rather than the true body end; the helper can therefore validate a declared body against caller-invented bounds that extend past the socket allocation
writes_without_output_bound.late_loop_bound: only after the copy, 0x13a9d..0x13ac6 compares cumulative declared input consumption with S; it neither prevents an out-of-input read/copy nor compares output-used with context+0xa8
writes_without_output_bound.nal_conversion: for each helper-accepted NAL, 0x13a3a stores a 4-byte Annex-B start code and 0x13a65 copies the declared NAL body, then advances output-used by 4+length
